_comment: LoopStar GENERATIVE material pack for G-FUNK (LP.6 lineage). Genre-authentic DNA for the on-device 'Make it new' generator (LoopStarMaterialEngine). The Swift binary is a SKELETON (RULE #1). Companion phrase pack: phrases/gfunk/. Source: docs/idiom-research/genre-hiphop.md section 3 (88-96 BPM, swung 16ths ~57% -> swing 0.14, fat kick + layered snare/clap backbeat, open hat at the and-of-4, clav/Rhodes rootless-9 comping, round Moog bass D1-D2, whiny square lead C5-C7). GM programs 0-based. Schema owner: LoopStarGenrePack.swift.
name: G-Funk
blurb: West-coast G-funk: a whiny high synth lead sliding over a two-chord minor-9 vamp, rubber Moog bass, lazy swung hats, and clav skank on the upbeats.

flavors.label: Dorian Cruise
flavors.blurb: The Dre shuttle: im9 to IV9, two bars each, clav skanking the upbeats forever.

flavors.label: Static Menace
flavors.blurb: One bare minor chord that never moves -- just the whiny lead and the bass doing the talking.

flavors.label: Quiet Storm
flavors.blurb: The R&B side: im9 to bVImaj7 on sustained Rhodes, no stabs, lights down.

flavors.label: Lowrider Lift
flavors.blurb: Actual movement for once: i-bVI-bVII-i climbing a bar at a time, brighter and pushed.

flavors.label: Talkbox Bounce
flavors.blurb: Zapp lineage in major: maj9 to m9 alternation with short, snappy clav chops.

arranger.llmStyleBrief: G-funk lives in one minor key, usually Dorian. Write two-chord vamps: im9 to IV9, im9 to bVII7, or im9 to bVImaj7 for the quiet-storm side. Hold each chord two bars. Ninths on everything, no ii-V motion, no modulation. The synth lead and rubber bass carry the melody; the changes just rock back and forth underneath.
